$comment: The consensus benchmark corpus. Every case is synthetic and public — no customer material, and nothing here describes a real person, venue or product. Each carries the defect it was BUILT to have, so agreement can be measured against something other than our own opinion. Cases are deliberately mixed: some are clean, some are broken in ways the Tribunal should catch, and a few are genuinely ambiguous, because a benchmark where every answer is obvious measures nothing.

cases.title: Launch thread — specific and grounded
cases.text: Tidepool turns a folder of field recordings into a mixed, mastered album. It ships with 40 presets, imports WAV and AIFF, and exports stems. It does not do noise removal — use Izotope for that first.

cases.title: Launch thread — unsupported superlative
cases.text: Tidepool is the fastest audio tool ever built and the only one professionals trust. Studies show it is 400% better than every competitor. Everyone who tries it switches immediately.

cases.title: Launch thread — generic AI filler
cases.text: In today's fast-paced world, innovation is key. Our solution leverages cutting-edge technology to deliver unparalleled value. Are you ready to take your workflow to the next level? The future is here.

cases.title: Toast — wrong voice for the occasion
cases.text: PURSUANT TO THE MARRIAGE HEREIN CELEBRATED, THE UNDERSIGNED WISHES TO FORMALLY REGISTER APPROVAL OF THE UNION, SUBJECT TO THE TERMS AND CONDITIONS SET FORTH BELOW. NOTWITHSTANDING THE FOREGOING, CONGRATULATIONS ARE EXTENDED.

cases.title: Toast — structureless
cases.text: So anyway I met Sam once and they were nice and then there was that thing with the car and also the dog and I forget the rest but congratulations I guess and the food here is good.

cases.title: Story page — plain and particular
cases.text: The kitchen table came from a house on Rye Lane that no longer exists. It has a burn mark near the left edge from a pan set down too fast in 1998. Every birthday since has been eaten around it.

cases.title: Launch thread — terse, arguably too terse
cases.text: Tidepool. Field recordings in, album out. Free while in beta.

cases.title: Guide — grounded claim with no source
cases.text: The museum opens at 9am on Sundays and free entry runs until noon. Parking on the north side is unrestricted after 10am. The cafe closes at 4pm sharp.

cases.title: Day plan — grounded and honest about uncertainty
cases.text: 10:00 arrive at the gardens (opening hours not confirmed — call ahead). 12:30 lunch nearby, 30 min walk allowed. 14:00 free time. Budget: entry 12 x 4 = 48, lunch ~25pp = 100, total ~148.

cases.title: Day plan — impossible schedule
cases.text: 14:00 lunch in the north quarter. 14:15 gallery tour in the south quarter, 40 minutes away. 14:30 boat departure from the harbour. 14:45 return for dessert at the first restaurant.

cases.title: Budget — does not add up
cases.text: Venue 400. Catering 650. Flowers 120. Music 300. Stationery 80. Total: 1,200. Deposit already paid: 500, so 600 remains outstanding.

cases.title: Plan — missing sources on every grounded claim
cases.text: The restaurant seats 40 and has step-free access. The weather that weekend will be mild and dry. The venue permits candles indoors and closes at 1am.

cases.title: Plan — claims a booking is confirmed
cases.text: Your table is booked and confirmed for 8pm, party of six, window seat guaranteed. The florist has accepted the order and delivery is locked in for Friday morning.

cases.title: Contingency — real fallbacks
cases.text: If it rains: move to the covered terrace (capacity 30, so 10 guests stand). If the band cancels: the venue's PA takes a phone via Bluetooth; playlist prepared. If numbers drop below 20: cancel the second catering tray by Thursday for a refund.

cases.title: Plan — thin but not wrong
cases.text: Morning: park. Afternoon: lunch and a walk. Evening: dinner somewhere in town. Budget roughly 150 for four people.
